//: Known-red UI tests, measured on origin/main.
Why this file exists: `pnpm test` used to exit 0 while 23 tests failed, so the
CI test step could not fail on a broken UI test (task 73h8). The exit code is
fixed, but the 23 failures below are genuinely red on main and were not
introduced by that fix. Rather than exclude their nine files wholesale -- which
would also stop gating the 98 tests in them that pass -- `scripts/vitest-ci.mjs`
runs the WHOLE suite and fails only on failures that are not listed here.
Consequences:
* A new failure anywhere in the suite, including inside these nine files,
turns the UI Frontend job red.
* Fixing a listed test prints a loud reminder to delete its line here. That is
a warning and not a failure on purpose, so a timing-sensitive test that
happens to pass on a fast runner cannot turn the gate red on its own.
* A truncated or crashed run -- no JSON report, or a test file that never
reported -- is a hard failure. That is the exact shape of the 73h8 defect.
* A file that reports `failed` with no failing test is a hard failure. That
is a collection error: the file never loaded and none of its tests ran.
`totalTests` below is LOAD-BEARING, not documentation. The gate fails when a
run collects fewer tests than it records, because the failure mode that
defeated the first version of this gate (task pxtd) removed 35 tests from the
run while leaving the failure count at exactly 23. Lower it deliberately, in
the same commit that deletes tests, and never to make a red run go green.
This list is a debt ledger. It must only ever shrink.
